crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Evidence Extraction Tables
children.blurb: Evidence extraction tables are the structured grids in which a systematic review records what each included study reported, one row per study and one column per item of interest.

children.name: Weighing the Scientific Consensus
children.blurb: Weighing the scientific consensus means judging how strongly a body of research supports a claim, rather than treating a single paper or a single summary as decisive.

children.name: Questioning Your Own Sources
children.blurb: Questioning your own sources is the practice of testing the evidence a literature review rests on before that evidence is used to support a conclusion.

children.name: Deep Research Agents and Landscape Scans
children.blurb: Deep research agents and landscape scans cover the use of AI systems to carry out multi step literature searches, gather sources, and assemble a structured view of what is known about a topic.

children.name: Translating Between Disciplines
children.blurb: Translating between disciplines is the work of moving a finding, method or term from the field that produced it into another field that can use it, without losing what it meant in the original.

sections.body: Literature review and evidence synthesis is the work of turning a pile of papers into a defensible account of what is known. In practice, AI is used to pull study details into structured tables, screen abstracts against inclusion criteria, cluster findings by method or population, and draft summaries that a human then checks. Deep research agents now run multi step searches across databases and the open web, returning cited reports rather than a list of links. The output is a first pass, not a verdict, and the useful systems are the ones that keep every claim tied to a source a reader can open.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Extraction and screening are largely solved for well formatted text, and models are good at finding passages that match a question. What is not solved is judgment: deciding whether two studies measure the same thing, whether a null result reflects a real absence of effect, or whether a body of work is large enough to support a claim. Models still fabricate citations, misread tables, and flatten disagreement into false balance or false consensus. The honest limit is that synthesis is an argument about evidence quality, and no current system can be trusted to make that argument unsupervised.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: Evidence Extraction Tables is the entry point for anyone who needs to get numbers and study characteristics out of papers and into a comparable form. Weighing the Scientific Consensus takes those extracted findings and asks how much weight a body of work can carry, which is where most reviews go wrong. Questioning Your Own Sources sits alongside it as the corrective, pushing a reader to test the papers they already trust rather than only the ones they doubt. Deep Research Agents and Landscape Scans covers the tooling for broad, fast sweeps when the goal is coverage rather than depth. Translating Between Disciplines is for the harder case where the relevant evidence lives in a field with different vocabulary, methods, and standards of proof, and it shows how to move a question across that boundary without losing its meaning.
